# **The Finishing Guide**

## **Introduction**
This document provides an overview of the process to complete various tasks and ensure a high-quality print output. The focus is on maintaining consistent appearance, typography, layout design, color management, image preparation, text handling and page quality throughout.

### **1. Typography & Typefaces**
#### a) Consistency in Fonts  
All text should be consistently formatted with one font family (e.g., Arial, Times New Roman). Use specific size specifications for each section as provided in the project scope or template guidelines.

#### b) Font Subsets/Supersets  
Consider using scalable fonts when necessary, especially if working with logos and brand-specific type faces that may become distorted at smaller sizes.

###### c) Case & Text Direction  
Use `title-cased` instead of `sentence-case`. Ensure texts are not mixed across sections unless explicitly instructed so.

###### d) Spacing & Line Heights  
Define line heights for paragraphs and headings within the document. If not specified, default values can be used from the chosen typeface.

###### e) Character Shapes & Styling Options  
Avoid overly decorative characters in favor of simple letters to enhance readability.

### **2. Layout Design Specifications**
#### a) Page Layouts & Margins  
Each main section's margins should remain constant for consistency with the overall project requirements. Define these margins clearly without specifying their exact dimensions.
